exposure: umbilical cord blood Vitamin D levels
mother's compliance to Vitamin D intake
outcome: rectovaginal colonization with Group B Streptococcus (GBS)
cohort: The study included 795 pregnant women whose maternal Vitamin D serum levels, umbilical cord blood Vitamin D levels, maternal GBS status, and compliance to Vitamin D intake were collected and examined retrospectively between November 2017 and May 2018.
finding: Low Vitamin D levels in maternal serum during early pregnancy and in umbilical cord blood are significantly associated with an increased risk of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonization in the third trimester of pregnancy.
